extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers of Registered Reports (Stage 1 protocol reviewers and Stage 2 results reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Peer-review rubric for evaluating Registered Reports at Stage 1 (protocol/pre-data) and Stage 2 (post-data execution and reporting), focusing on methodological validity, adherence to the registered protocol, and outcome-neutral assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1A. Scientific Validity of the Research Question
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the research question is scientifically justifiable through theory, application, or evidence base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjective judgments about importance or novelty are explicitly excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1B. Logic and Rationale of the Hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates coherence and credibility of a priori hypotheses; hypotheses must follow directly from theory and be worthy of investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesis specification is optional (exploratory Registered Reports are allowed) but where present, hypotheses must be testable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1C. Soundness and Feasibility of the Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of study procedures and design choices, critical design features (validity, blinding, randomisation, controls), analysis plans (statistical tests, model specification), and for hypothesis tests: sampling plans and power analysis (or Bayesian equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review whether design and analysis demonstrate the ability to detect or rule out the predicted effect; consider feasibility of proposed procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1D. Methodological Clarity and Detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the clarity and degree of methodological detail is sufficient to closely replicate the proposed study procedures and to prevent undisclosed analytical flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess if the protocol gives enough procedural, analytic, and decision-rule detail to enable replication and to constrain researcher degrees of freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1E. Outcome-Neutral Quality Checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors have specified sufficient outcome-neutral conditions that must hold for the design to inform the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include positive controls (manipulation checks), absence of floor/ceiling effects, a priori sample-quality criteria, and successful instrument validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2A. Data Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines whether the data meet the prespecified outcome-neutral conditions and are adequate to test the hypotheses or address the research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adherence to the pre-specified quality checks and whether the realized data support valid inference under the registered plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2B. Introduction Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Introduction, rationale, and stated hypotheses are the same as the approved Stage 1 submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted changes are tense adjustments and typographical corrections only; substantive changes to rationale or hypotheses are not permitted without approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2C. Protocol Adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors adhered precisely to the registered study procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor deviations require recommender approval; substantial deviations require resubmission. Reviewers should evaluate whether deviations compromise validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2D. Quality of Unregistered (Exploratory) Analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether any exploratory analyses added beyond the registered plan are justified, methodologically sound, and clearly distinguished from preregistered confirmatory analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploratory analyses must be motivated (not fishing) and must not be used to draw confirmatory inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2E. Justification of Conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors' conclusions are justified given the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should disregard perceived importance, novelty, or conclusiveness of results; focus on whether conclusions follow from the data and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome-blind reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must not let the direction of the result influence the recommendation; in-principle acceptance is granted at Stage 1 before any results exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain evaluative focus on methodological validity rather than positive/negative/null outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No 'interestingness' rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty or significance are not grounds for rejection at either stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review criteria exclude subjective judgments about importance or novelty when deciding acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No 'I would have done it differently' mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must distinguish suggestions from required changes; required changes must be tied to validity, not reviewer preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not convert desirable-but-nonessential preferences into mandatory requirements; tie any required revisions explicitly to threats to validity or interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent scoring rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers' Stage 1 scores anchor the in-principle acceptance and are visible to the author and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring should be transparent and justifiable, since it determines in-principle acceptance and is part of the public record.
